title: Theo and the Harbor
premise: In 1903, Rafael Marchetti keeps the harbor light alone after her husband's drowning, hiding her late father's forbidden workshop of forged maritime papers beneath the lamp room. When a stranger named Ivo arrives with a letter in her father's unmistakable hand—written years after his reported death—Rafael learns the old man may still be alive, and that the documents she has been burning were evidence in a smuggling ring that cost her husband his life. As the great storms close the harbor and the authorities close in, Rafael must choose between destroying the workshop and her family's name, or finishing her father's final ledger and exposing the truth. She finishes it, testifies at the inquiry, and leaves the light to a chosen successor rather than an inherited lie.
about_author: Theo Zhou is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal shipping records before turning to fiction. They write about people whose lives are measured in what can be carried.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine storm season opens; we learn she measures everything by what can be carried when evacuation orders come—the lens cloth, the logbook, nothing from the locked room below. Emotional beat: disciplined grief, a life pared to essentials.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Ivo arrives half-drowned, carrying a water-stained letter addressed to Rafael in her father's handwriting—dated three years after his burial at sea. Rafael's POV. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Rafael's POV. How her father taught her forgery as 'keeping ships honest,' how her husband Tomas discovered the smuggling ledgers, how he drowned weeks later. Emotional beat: guilt reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Cargo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He claims to be her father's courier, but Rafael finds a customs seal on his belongings linking him to the men Tomas suspected. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before trust is earned.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: The harbor authority orders the light decommissioned for the winter storms; Rafael has until the last supply boat to clear out. Rafael's POV. Emotional beat: the deadline made literal—finish the work or lose it forever.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Working by lamplight, Rafael reconstructs her father's final ledger and realizes he faked his death to finish it—and that Ivo was sent not to help her but to retrieve and burn it. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: betrayal inside hope.

chapters.title: The Last Supply Boat
chapters.summary: Ivo confesses: her father is alive, hidden, dying, and wanted the ledger delivered or destroyed by Rafael's own hand. Rafael must decide before the boat sails without them. Ivo's POV. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Harbor
chapters.summary: Climax. The great storm hits early; the light must be kept burning manually while the harbormaster's men come for the workshop. Rafael chooses to keep both the light and the ledger, nearly losing her life in the lamp room. Rafael's POV. Emotional beat: refusal to be invisible.

chapters.title: The Inquiry
chapters.summary: Rafael testifies, naming the smugglers and clearing Tomas's name; her father, brought ashore to confirm the ledger, dies two days later having heard her forgive him. Rafael's POV. Emotional beat: truth as costly inheritance, finally accepted.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Spring. Rafael trains a young successor, packs one bag, and leaves the workshop standing—not burned, not hidden—as an archive anyone may read. Final image: her walking the harbor road with almost nothing, carrying everything. Rafael's POV. Emotional beat: release.
